bans.title: No grid backgrounds
bans.rule: Do not apply grid, graph-paper, dot-grid, or blueprint patterns as a section or page background, whether drawn with `background-image`, repeating gradients, SVG patterns, or a canvas overlay.
bans.instead: Use a flat surface token, a single subtle gradient, or genuine spatial structure built from spacing and dividers.

bans.title: No status conveyed by a left border color
bans.rule: Do not signal state — success, warning, error, info, active, selected, priority — with a colored `border-left` or any single colored edge stripe on cards, rows, alerts, or list items.
bans.instead: Use an explicit status element that carries text, such as a badge or label, paired with an icon and color. Color must never be the only channel that carries the status.

bans.title: No letters used as icons
bans.rule: Do not build an icon out of a letter, initial, or monogram: a character in a circle or rounded square standing in for an avatar, a logo, a brand mark, a category glyph, or a list bullet.
bans.instead: Use a real icon from `ui/icons/*` or the target project's existing icon set, an actual image or logo asset when one exists, or a plain text label when no icon is warranted.

bans.title: No mono accent eyebrow above a heading
bans.rule: Do not open a section, hero, or page with the eyebrow stack: a small monospaced, accent-colored, often uppercase or tracked-out label, then a larger heading beneath it, then a paragraph of supporting description. The ban covers the whole three-part pattern and the mono accent eyebrow on its own, however it is labelled — kicker, overline, tagline, section tag.
bans.instead: Lead with the heading itself and let the description follow. When the section genuinely needs a category marker, carry it in navigation, a breadcrumb, a tab, or a badge in the project's body font — not as a decorative line of mono accent text stacked above the title.

entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Place more than one primary button in the same view; this dilutes the visual hierarchy. Use the destructive variant without a confirmation step for irreversible actions like deleting data. Use a button for navigation. If it only takes the user to another page, use a link instead. Buttons are for actions like saving, deleting, or submitting.

entries.title: Astryx Button Group

entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Don't mix wildly different actions. A Save button next to a Delete button in the same group is confusing. Don't use ButtonGroup for navigation. Use SegmentedControl or TabList for switching between views. Don't nest ButtonGroups. If you need multiple groups, place them side by side with a gap. Don't disable the group to show that an action is in flight. A disabled member drops focus, so a keyboard user loses their place; leave the group enabled and show progress on the button that started the work.

entries.title: Astryx Segmented Control

Use for simple on/off states; use ToggleButton instead. ToggleButton can be toggled on or off independently, while SegmentedControl enforces a single selection from a group. Wrap a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

entries.title: Accordion
entries.useWhen: A disclosure / accordion / collapsible section whose panel grows and shrinks in height when toggled, with the header chevron flipping between a downward "v" and an upward "^". Use for settings groups, FAQs, filter sections, "show more" details — any header + collapsible body. Height animates via `grid-template-rows: 0fr ↔ 1fr`, so there's **no JS height measuring** and content of any size animates cleanly. The chevron flips vertically (`scaleY`) from a "v" to a "^", passing through a flat line at the midpoint. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Avatar Group Hover
entries.useWhen: Hovering an item in a horizontal stack (avatar row, chip group, badge cluster, segmented button) should lift the hovered item, gently lift its neighbors with a power-falloff, then snap everything back with an overshoot spring on `mouseleave`. Direction-aware easing (clean ease-in on hover, bouncy ease-out on return) is what gives the group its springy, physical feel. Equally good for: pill stacks in a tag editor, chips in a filter bar, reaction-emoji rows, anywhere a horizontal row benefits from a "comb" interaction signal. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Card Resize
entries.useWhen: Tweening a container's width or height when its layout state changes (compact ↔ expanded card, collapsing panel, list row toggling extra detail). Pure CSS — no JS required beyond the class toggle that drives the size change. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Card Tilt
entries.useWhen: A card / tile / media surface that tilts in 3D toward the pointer while hovered, with a soft light "glare" tracking the cursor across it. Use for product cards, credit / membership cards, feature tiles, cover art — anything that should feel physical and reactive on hover. Pointer-only (skips touch) and flattens under reduced motion. The pointer is tracked on an **outer flat wrapper** (`.t-tilt`) that never transforms, so the tilting card can't rotate its own edges out from under the cursor (which causes hover flicker). The inner `.t-tilt-card` is the element that actually rotates. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Checkbox Check
entries.useWhen: A checkbox needs a clear completion cue: fill the box, then draw its checkmark. Source: transitions.dev CSS tab; the site has no React tab for this newer free transition.

entries.title: Error State Shake
entries.useWhen: Form validation feedback — invalid email, wrong password, missing required field, mismatched confirmation. The input shakes left/right with overshoot, the border switches to error color, and a message reveals beneath. After a hold timer (long enough to read the message), border + message fade back to neutral. Optional: typing into the input cancels the auto-revert immediately. The `t-` snippet is also a fit for any "this is wrong, try again" moment that needs a percussive hint without an OS-level alert — a wrong-PIN field on a lock screen, a duplicate-tag warning in a tag editor, a "name already taken" username field. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Icon Swap
entries.useWhen: Cross-fading two icons in the same slot — hamburger ↔ close, sun ↔ moon, play ↔ pause, expand ↔ collapse. Both icons stay in the DOM stacked in the same grid cell. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Input Clear Dissolve
entries.useWhen: Clearing a text field — search box, filter input, any field with a clear (×) button. The typed text flies down + blurs + fades while a soft per-word streak ignites under each word, and the placeholder falls in from above. Per-frame JS is required: the streak envelope and per-word gradient stack cannot be expressed as static @keyframes. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Learn More Hover
entries.useWhen: A compact “learn more” action needs a restrained hover cue rather than a separate loading or navigation animation. Source: transitions.dev CSS tab; the site has no React tab for this newer free transition.

entries.title: Like Button
entries.useWhen: A lightweight like/favourite control should acknowledge a new selection with a heart fill, pop, and particle burst. Source: transitions.dev CSS tab; the site has no React tab for this newer free transition.

entries.title: Menu Dropdown
entries.useWhen: Contextual menus, dropdowns, popovers — anything that opens from a trigger and should visually grow from that trigger's position. Origin-aware via `data-origin` (top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-*). Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Modal
entries.useWhen: Modal dialogs and full-overlay surfaces that scale up from center. Use when the surface is conceptually "on top of" the page rather than anchored to a trigger. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Notification Badge
entries.useWhen: A small badge appearing on top of a trigger (bell, inbox, button). Slides in diagonally and pops the dot independently of the trigger so the trigger itself never moves. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Number Pop In
entries.useWhen: Counters, prices, balances, or any number that updates and should re-enter from a direction with blur. Each character animates independently and the last two digits stagger so decimals feel alive without looking chaotic. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Page Side By Side
entries.useWhen: Sliding between two full pages or screens that live side-by-side: list ↔ detail, step 1 ↔ step 2 in a wizard. Page 1 exits left, page 2 exits right. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Panel Reveal
entries.useWhen: A panel that slides into view inside an existing container — e.g. detail panel inside a card, expanding section. Combines a short translate, opacity, and a 2px cross-blur so a half-height travel still reads as a full open. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Plus Menu Morph
entries.useWhen: A small circular trigger (a "+" FAB, a compose button, an add-action affordance) that **morphs into the menu / panel it opens** instead of popping a separate surface next to it. The button's box grows in width / height and relaxes its corner radius into a rounded panel while the plus icon cross-fades + rotates out and the menu content slides in. Reach for this over **menu dropdown** when the trigger and the surface are the *same* element (the button becomes the panel). Use plain **menu dropdown** when the surface is a distinct popover that merely grows from the trigger's corner. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Shimmer Text
entries.useWhen: A loading / "thinking" label that shimmers — streaming status, "Generating…", any in-progress copy that should feel alive without a spinner. Pure CSS: duplicate the string into `data-text` on `.t-shimmer` and tune `--shimmer-base` / `--shimmer-highlight` per theme. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Skeleton Reveal
entries.useWhen: A placeholder that loads then reveals real content — list rows, cards, profile headers. The skeleton pulses, then both layers cross-fade with a matching cross-blur. Bring your own bars / avatar / text; the skeleton stays in the same slot as the content so the swap is layout-free. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Spinning Counter
entries.useWhen: A compact numeric value should visibly roll to its next value, such as a score, price, or live count. Source: transitions.dev CSS tab; the site has no React tab for this newer free transition.

entries.title: Success Check
entries.useWhen: Confirming a completed action — payment processed, file uploaded, message sent, form saved. The icon fades in, rotates upright, settles with a Y-bob, and (for SVG icons) draws its path stroke. Use whenever a status changes from "pending / unknown" to "success" and you want the moment to feel earned rather than instantaneous. The snippet covers the **appear transition only** — bring your own hide behavior (e.g. unmount, opacity:0, or a custom exit). This is intentional: success states are usually persistent, and a soft fade-out is rarely worth the extra DOM/JS surface. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Tabs Sliding
entries.useWhen: A segmented control / tab bar where the active pill slides between options — view switchers, filter segments, small mutually-exclusive button sets. JS writes the active tab's `offsetLeft` / `offsetWidth` onto the pill; CSS owns the tween. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Text States Swap
entries.useWhen: Swapping the text of a status indicator in place — "Processing…" → "Done", "Save" → "Saved". The old text exits up with blur, the new text enters from below. Source: transitions.dev — React tab.

entries.title: Texts Reveal

Pass a name prop; Icon uses icon (not name) to specify which icon to render.

entries.avoidWhen:
Override size and weight when a semantic type already matches; extra overrides fight the theme and break when themes change. Skip heading levels in the document outline; go h1 then h2 then h3, never h1 then h3. Use raw HTML tags like

,

–

, or for text; Text and Heading apply the correct theme tokens automatically. Pass a variant prop; Text does not have a variant prop. Use type for semantic styling (body, label, large, supporting, code) or use Heading for headings. Use Text for headings; use Heading with a level prop (1–6) for section titles and headings.

entries.avoidWhen: Don't use Thumbnail for non-image file types like PDFs or spreadsheets; use a file attachment component with an appropriate icon instead. Don't omit alt text when a src is provided; screen readers need a description of the image content, not just the file name from label.
entries.provides: Image, Placeholder, Remove button, Upload overlay, Skeleton
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Timer
entries.useWhen: Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Do not use Timer for dates, time zones, or relative calendar language; use Timestamp instead. Do not add aria-live unless hearing an announcement every tick is appropriate for the specific task.

entries.title: Astryx Timestamp
entries.useWhen: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format. Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts. Don't disable the hover card on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago". Don't stack many zones into one card; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well. Don't pass a fixed-offset abbreviation like "EST" as timezoneID; it is a valid identifier but never observes daylight saving, so it reads an hour wrong for half the year. Use the region id, "America/New_York".
entries.provides: Formatted text, Hover card, Hover card row, Copy button
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Token
entries.useWhen: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections.

entries.avoidWhen: Don't use tokens for primary actions or navigation; use Button or Link instead. Tokens are for displaying metadata, not triggering workflows. Stick to two or three meaningful colors so the palette stays scannable.

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart
entries.useWhen: Chart lays out one or more mark definitions against shared responsive x and y scales.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use color as the only way to distinguish series or communicate status. Pair color with labels, mark shapes, direct annotations, or another visible cue. Reuse one mark definition object across multiple Chart instances. Mark definitions currently carry per-chart layout metadata and are single-use.
entries.provides: Header, Plot, Grid and axes, Legend, Tooltip and interactions, Data table
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/charts and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart Axis
entries.useWhen: ChartAxis renders tick labels and optional edge and tick lines from the scales owned by a parent Chart.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use axis labels or a pointer tooltip as the only way to obtain important values. Give Chart an accessible name and preserve an equivalent data view or summary. Hide the edge line while showing tick marks. showTicks intentionally keeps the line visible so each mark has a grounded edge.
entries.provides: Axis edge line, Tick marks, Tick labels
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/charts and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart Grid
entries.useWhen: ChartGrid draws horizontal and vertical guide lines from the scales owned by a parent Chart.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use grid lines as the only way to communicate a value or distinction. Keep meaningful chart information in labels, marks, and the parent Chart alternative. Expect tickCount to thin categorical band centers. It requests density only for continuous scales; categorical vertical guides render once per band.
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/charts and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart Legend
entries.useWhen: ChartLegend pairs series labels with decorative mark-shaped color swatches.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use the legend as the chart’s only text alternative. Give the parent Chart an accessible name and preserve an equivalent data view or summary when the data requires one. Assume arbitrary series colors will remain distinguishable in every theme. Verify the complete chart and legend together against the surfaces where they render.
entries.provides: Legend list, Legend entry, Series swatch, Series label
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/charts and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart Swatch
entries.useWhen: ChartSwatch renders the small decorative mark that pairs a chart series color with its visible label.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use ChartSwatch as the accessible name or data alternative for a series. Its surrounding legend, tooltip, or chart must provide that information. Rely on arbitrary colors alone when multiple same-shaped series must be matched across a chart. Verify the complete chart and its labels together.
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/charts and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Charts Chart Tooltip

entries.title: Astryx Calendar
entries.useWhen: Calendar lets the user pick a date or date range from a month grid.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use a calendar for dates far in the past or future like a birth date. A text input is faster for open-ended entry. Disable large blocks of dates without context. The user should understand why dates are unavailable.
entries.provides: Month header, Day grid, Selected day, Today marker
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Checkbox Input
entries.useWhen: CheckboxInput toggles a single on/off value.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use a checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioList when only one option can be selected. Use a checkbox for actions that take effect immediately; use a toggle switch or button instead. Wrap a disabled checkbox in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Checkbox List
entries.useWhen: CheckboxList shows a small group of checkboxes so users can turn several options on or off at once.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Show a CheckboxList when the user can only pick one thing; that is what RadioList is for. Put buttons or links inside the trailing slot (endContent); the whole row is already tappable, so a nested button creates two competing click targets. Wrap a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.provides: Group, Group label, Description, Options list, Option row, Checkbox, Option label, Option description, End content, Spinner, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Complex Selector
entries.useWhen: Use ComplexSelector when a selection needs richer custom content than a Selector option row.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Do not rebuild trigger ARIA, popover focus management, or changeAction handling in product code. Do not use ComplexSelector for a plain single-column text list; use Selector instead.
entries.provides: Field, Trigger, Icon-rendered start icon, Caller-rendered start content, Indicator icon, Popup
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Date Input
entries.useWhen: DateInput lets the user type or pick a date from a calendar popover.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date. Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious. Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates. Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.provides: Label, Text input, Calendar icon, Calendar popover, Clear button, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Date Range Input
entries.useWhen: DateRangeInput lets users select a start and end date from a dual-month calendar popover.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use DateRangeInput when only a single date is needed; use DateInput instead. Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the purpose obvious. Wrap a disabled DateRangeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.provides: Label, Field surface, Trigger button, Calendar icon, Calendar popover, Preset sidebar, Preset button, Clear button, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Date Time Input
entries.useWhen: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead. Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead. Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious. Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.provides: Label, Date input, Calendar icon, Date picker, Time input, Time options popover, Clear button, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Field
entries.useWhen: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Nest Field around styled inputs such as TextInput, Typeahead, Select, DateInput, or TextArea; those components already render their own Field shell. Use the attached status variant on non-bordered controls such as sliders, switches, or checkboxes; use detached so the message does not overlap the control. Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field. Hide the label without providing an alternative way for the user to understand the field purpose.
entries.provides: Label, Description, Control slot, Status message, Optional/Required indicator, Label tooltip
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Field Status
entries.useWhen: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.
entries.provides: Message box, Detached icon, Message text
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx File Input
entries.useWhen: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1. Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads. Don't wrap a disabled FileInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.
entries.provides: Label, Description, Drop zone, Upload icon, Placeholder, File name display, Clear button, Spinner, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Indicator
entries.useWhen: Indicators are the componentized selection visuals shared by CheckboxInput, RadioList, and menu selection rows.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Thread hover or pressed state in as props. Interaction state reaches an indicator through the owner's CSS ancestor marker, so hovering the row tints the control with no props involved. Assume you are only mounted when selected. The host renders its indicator unconditionally and passes state, in every state; that is what lets a replacement draw where the default draws nothing (a radio's empty circle on an unchosen row). Drawing nothing in a state is a decision the indicator makes, not one the host makes for it.
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Input Group
entries.useWhen: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Don't put multiple text inputs in one group; use separate fields instead. Don't use InputGroup for unrelated inputs; it's for a single input with decorations. Don't use InputGroup with TextArea, Slider, Switch, CheckboxInput, or RadioList.
entries.provides: Label, Prefix addon, Input, Suffix addon, Status message
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Lab List Input
entries.useWhen: ListInput edits a compact, ordered collection of records with consistent fields, built-in add and remove actions, and optional reordering.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use for seven or more records or more than three simple fields per record; use a Table or a dedicated editing flow instead. Prevent removal solely to enforce a minimum count; allow the action and explain the resulting requirement with list-level validation.
entries.provides: Label and description, First-record field labels, Record fields, Remove action, Reorder handle, Empty state, Add action, Validation messages

entries.title: Astryx Lab Transfer List Selector
entries.useWhen: Use TransferListSelector by default for medium-to-large, inspectable sets where membership and selected order need explicit control.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example

entries.avoidWhen: Use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation. They supplement a sidebar or top nav, not replace it. Show breadcrumbs on top-level pages that have no parent; they add clutter without helping the user. Let the trail grow beyond 5 levels. If you need more, consider simplifying the page hierarchy instead. Mirror a separator the bidi algorithm already mirrors. An angle-quote glyph such as › is Bidi_Mirrored, so it flips under RTL on its own and rtlStyles.mirror would flip it back. An arrow glyph such as → and any Icon separator are not, so those do need rtlStyles.mirror through xstyle.

Durations ("6h window"), counts ("12 trigger types"), dates, and descriptions are not statuses or categories; use description text (Text with type="supporting") instead. Repeat the same badge in every row of a table or list. entries.title: Astryx Card
entries.useWhen: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default. Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack. Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all. Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead. Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css

entries.title: Astryx Carousel
entries.useWhen: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width.
entries.medium: React 19 + TypeScript + StyleX (prebuilt CSS); static HTML + CSS per example
entries.avoidWhen: Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold. Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace. Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.
entries.provides: Scroll container, Items, Fade edges, Navigation buttons
entries.requires: React 19 with @astryxdesign/core and a theme, or the static HTML with ui/_sources/astryx/frame.css
